newsitem.title: UK: Moody's sees only small chance of EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Moody's sees only small chance of EMU delay.

text.p: A senior analyst at Moody's Investors Service said on Thursday that the credit rating agency gave the highest probability of European monetary union starting on time in 1999, and saw only a small chance of a delay. "We try to factor in a variety of scenarios, but the highest probability (is) that EMU will go ahead on time," said David Levey, co-head of Moody's sovereign risk unit.

In an interview with Reuters following a report on the rating implications of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU), Levey said the agency currently was "pretty certain" that eight countries would be in the first wave of EMU.
Levey said these countries would likely be Belgium, Austria, Finland, France, Germany, Netherlands, Ireland and Luxembourg.
He said there was only the smallest probablility that EMU would collapse altogether.
"There's a strong dynamic pushing the process forward...but we're not basing our ratings on absolute certainty -- we're hedging out bets," he said.

Levey declined to comment on the likelihood of Italy joining EMU in the first wave but said whether it was in or out, Moody's assessment that participating countries' foreign currency debt ceilings would be Aaa, would remain unchanged.
"If Italy is out (of EMU)...but is moving towards EMU, the foreign currency debt ceiling will begin to adjust (towards Aaa)," said Levey.
"Perhaps even the government bond rating may be affected, but not necessarily just because of EMU...but indirectly," he added.
